# Setup
This file reproduces all analyses and figures for the paper Nielsen, K., Ding, J., Ejsing, M., Sekara, V., & Dablander, F. (2026). Personal climate agency in a high-income context. All derived variables come from `data_cleaning.Rmd`.

```{r packages}

  dplyr::arrange, dplyr::lag,
  lmerTest::lmer, lme4::glmer
)

looks_right <- function(p) {
  !is.null(p) && !is.na(p) && nzchar(p) && dir.exists(p) &&
    (file.exists(file.path(p, "data_rudersdal.csv")) ||
     file.exists(file.path(p, "clean", "data_clean_person.rds")))
}

project_data <- getwd()
clean_dir   <- file.path(project_data, "data", "clean")     # written by the cleaning script
output_dir  <- file.path(project_data, "output")    # tables and SI figures
figure_dir  <- file.path(project_data, "figures")   # D3 sources + JSON

for (d in c(clean_dir, output_dir, figure_dir)) {
  dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Cleaned data. Produced by data_cleaning.Rmd, which is run once here if the
# files are absent. Delete the files in clean/ to force a re-clean.
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
clean_files <- c("data_clean_person.rds", "data_clean_long.rds", "constants.rds")

cleaning_rmd <- c(
  file.path(project_data, "data_cleaning.Rmd"),
  here::here("data_cleaning.Rmd")
)
cleaning_rmd <- cleaning_rmd[file.exists(cleaning_rmd)][1]

missing <- clean_files[!file.exists(file.path(clean_dir, clean_files))]

if (length(missing) > 0) {
  if (is.na(cleaning_rmd)) {
    stop("Cleaned data not found in ", clean_dir,
         "\nMissing: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         "\nand data_cleaning.Rmd was not found. Run the cleaning script, ",
         "or place it in ", project_data)
  }
  message("Cleaned data not found; running ", basename(cleaning_rmd), " once...")
  callr::r(
    function(rmd, project_dir) {
      setwd(project_dir)
      rmarkdown::render(
        input = rmd,
        quiet = TRUE,
        envir = new.env(parent = globalenv())
      )
    },
    args = list(cleaning_rmd, project_data),
    show = TRUE
  )

  still <- clean_files[!file.exists(file.path(clean_dir, clean_files))]
  if (length(still) > 0) {
    stop("The cleaning script ran but did not write: ", paste(still, collapse = ", "),
         "\nCheck that it saves to ", clean_dir)
  }
}

  "13" = "Promote change in organisation", "14" = "Be a climate role model",
  "15" = "Talk with family/friends",       "16" = "Vote for pro-climate politicians",
  "17" = "Sign petitions/contact politicians", "18" = "Participate in demonstrations"
)

id_by_name <- df_long |>
  distinct(behaviour_id, behaviour_name) |>

clean_names <- c(

# Analysis populations, defined once
df_relevant <- df_long |> filter(action_status != "Not relevant")
df_untaken  <- df_long |>

  group_by(behaviour_id) |>
  mutate(
    # Standardise expected QoL only among respondents who have not yet taken

    qol_expected_z = if (sum(!is.na(qol)) > 1) {
      as.numeric(scale(qol))
    } else {
      NA_real_
    }
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# Employed respondents with a work-position classification, reused below
df_emp <- df_long |>
  filter(is_employed == "Employed", !is.na(leadership_cat)) |>
  mutate(
    leadership_cat = factor(leadership_cat,
      levels = c("No decision authority", "Professional/administrative",

    is_organisational = factor(

role_sizes <- df_long |>
```

## Effects helpers

Every predictor is fitted in its own model, adjusted for the structural
predictors (the "individual regressions" in the text). `multiple = TRUE` fits all
predictors together (SI).

```{r helpers}
# Contrasts: continuous predictors +1 SD; gender_bin explicitly 0 -> 1.
contrast_spec <- function(vars) {
  setNames(lapply(vars, function(v) if (v == "gender_bin") c(0, 1) else 1), vars)
}

adjust_for <- function(p) {
  adj <- c(setdiff(c("gender_bin", "age_z", "income_filled_z"), p), "income_status")
  if (p == "prestige_filled_z") adj <- c(adj, "prestige_status")
  adj
}

fit_effects <- function(data, outcome, preds,
                        family = c("binomial", "gaussian"),
                        level  = c("role", "behaviour"),
                        multiple = FALSE) {

  family <- match.arg(family)
  level  <- match.arg(level)

  fam <- if (family == "binomial") {
    binomial("logit")
  } else {
    gaussian()
  }

  by <- if (level == "role") {
    "behaviour_role"
  } else {
    "behaviour_name"
  }

  re <- if (level == "role") {
    "(1 | response_id) + (1 | behaviour_id)"
  } else {
    "(1 | response_id)"
  }

  one <- function(focal, adj) {

    rhs <- paste0(
      "(",
      paste(focal, collapse = " + "),
      ") * ",
      by
    )

    if (length(adj)) {
      rhs <- paste(
        rhs,
        "+",
        paste(adj, collapse = " + ")
      )
    }

    f <- as.formula(
      paste(
        outcome,
        "~",
        rhs,
        "+",
        re
      )
    )

    d <- drop_na(
      data,
      all_of(c(outcome, focal, adj))
    )

    m <- glmmTMB(
      f,
      family = fam,
      data = d
    )

    vs <- contrast_spec(focal)

    overall <- avg_comparisons(
      m,
      variables = vs,
      type = "response"
    ) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(level = "Overall")

    by_lvl <- avg_comparisons(
      m,
      variables = vs,
      by = by,
      type = "response"
    ) |>
      as_tibble() |>
      mutate(
        level = as.character(.data[[by]])
      )

    bind_rows(
      overall,
      by_lvl
    ) |>
      transmute(
        term,
        level,
        estimate,
        conf.low,
        conf.high,
        n_obs = nrow(d)
      )
  }

  out <- if (multiple) {

    one(
      preds,
      c(
        "income_status",
        "prestige_status"
      )
    )

  } else {

    map_dfr(
      preds,
      function(p) {
        one(
          p,
          adjust_for(p)
        )
      }
    )
  }

  out |>
    mutate(
      outcome = outcome,
      Predictor = unname(clean_names[term])
    )
}
```

## Sensitivity check against self-reported consumer behaviour

Reported before the climate action items. If "already taken" is understood correctly,
respondents who report having cut flights, meat or driving should report lower
current levels than those for whom the action is relevant but not yet taken.

```{r s1-sensitivity}
baseline_map <- tribble(
  ~behaviour_id, ~baseline_var,      ~baseline_label,
  8L,            "driving",          "Annual kilometres driven (category)",
  3L,            "flying_frequency", "Number of one-way flights",
  4L,            "red_meat",         "Red meat consumption frequency",
  7L,            "white_meat",       "White meat consumption frequency"
)

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Validate "Already taken" against separately reported behaviour
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

tab_validation <- baseline_map |>
  pmap_dfr(function(behaviour_id, baseline_var, baseline_label) {

    d <- df_long |>
      filter(behaviour_id == !!behaviour_id) |>
      # Standardise using all respondents with valid data for the behaviour,
      # before restricting to the two action-status groups
      mutate(y = as.numeric(scale(.data[[baseline_var]])))

    desc <- d |>
      filter(action_status %in% c("Relevant, not taken", "Already taken")) |>
      group_by(action_status) |>
      summarise(
        n = sum(!is.na(.data[[baseline_var]])),
        mean = mean(.data[[baseline_var]], na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )

    d_model <- d |>
      filter(
        action_status %in% c("Relevant, not taken", "Already taken"),
        !is.na(y)
      ) |>
      mutate(
        taken = as.integer(action_status == "Already taken")
      )

    fit <- lm(y ~ taken, data = d_model)
    ci <- confint(fit)["taken", ]

    tibble(
      action = short_labels[[as.character(behaviour_id)]],
      measure = baseline_label,
      n_not_taken = desc$n[
        desc$action_status == "Relevant, not taken"
      ],
      mean_not_taken = desc$mean[
        desc$action_status == "Relevant, not taken"
      ],
      n_taken = desc$n[
        desc$action_status == "Already taken"
      ],
      mean_taken = desc$mean[
        desc$action_status == "Already taken"
      ],
      diff_sd = coef(fit)[["taken"]],
      conf.low = ci[1],
      conf.high = ci[2]
    )
  })

# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Supplementary Table 2
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------

tab_validation_ft <- tab_validation |>
  transmute(
    Action = action,
    n_not_taken = n_not_taken,
    mean_not_taken = mean_not_taken,
    n_taken = n_taken,
    mean_taken = mean_taken,
    difference = sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)",
      diff_sd, conf.low, conf.high
    )
  )

ft_validation <- flextable(tab_validation_ft) |>

  set_header_labels(
    Action = "Action",
    n_not_taken = "n",
    mean_not_taken = "Mean",
    n_taken = "n",
    mean_taken = "Mean",
    difference = "Difference (95% CI), SD"
  ) |>

  add_header_row(
    values = c(
      "",
      "Relevant, not taken",
      "Already taken",
      ""
    ),
    colwidths = c(1, 2, 2, 1)
  ) |>

  merge_at(i = 1:2, j = 1, part = "header") |>
  merge_at(i = 1:2, j = 6, part = "header") |>

  colformat_double(
    j = c("mean_not_taken", "mean_taken"),
    digits = 2
  ) |>

  border_remove() |>

  hline_top(
    part = "header",
    border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 1)
  ) |>
  hline(
    i = 2,
    part = "header",
    border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 0.75)
  ) |>
  hline_bottom(
    part = "body",
    border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 1)
  ) |>

  font(fontname = "Arial", part = "all") |>
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  bold(part = "header") |>
```

# Socioeconomic differences in the opportunity space

We examine whether the probability that an action is part of respondents'
opportunity space varies with socioeconomic and demographic characteristics,
and whether these associations differ across roles.

## Main models 

```{r s2-models}

# Income non-response is handled using the missingness indicator and
# mean-filled standardised income variables created in the cleaning script.
df_m2 <- df_long |>
  drop_na(
    is_relevant,
    age_z,
    gender_bin,
    income_status,
    income_filled_z,
    is_employed,
    behaviour_role
  )

message(
  "Participants in main models: ",
  n_distinct(df_m2$response_id),
  " / ",
  n_distinct(df_long$response_id)
)

message(
  "Person-action observations in main models: ",
  nrow(df_m2),
  " / ",
  nrow(df_long)
)

form0 <- is_relevant ~
  1 +
  (1 | response_id) +
  (1 | behaviour_id)

# Additive model: associations assumed to be common across roles
form1 <- is_relevant ~
  age_z +
  gender_bin +
  income_status +
  income_filled_z +
  is_employed +
  behaviour_role +
  (1 | response_id) +
  (1 | behaviour_id)

# Interaction model: associations allowed to differ across roles
form2 <- is_relevant ~
  (age_z +
    gender_bin +
    income_status +
    income_filled_z +
    is_employed
  ) * behaviour_role +
  (1 | response_id) +
  (1 | behaviour_id)

m0 <- glmmTMB(
  form0,
  family = binomial("logit"),
  data = df_m2
)

m1 <- glmmTMB(
  form1,
  family = binomial("logit"),
  data = df_m2
)

m2 <- glmmTMB(
  form2,
  family = binomial("logit"),
  data = df_m2
)

anova(m0, m1, m2)

map(
  list(m0 = m0, m1 = m1, m2 = m2),
  r2_nakagawa
)

check_collinearity(m2)
```

## Model comparison: Supplementary Table 3 

```{r s2-model-comparison}

# Document why the role-specific interaction model is preferred.
lrt_s2 <- anova(m0, m1, m2) |>
  as.data.frame()

r2_s2 <- imap_dfr(
  list(
    "Null model" = m0,
    "Additive model" = m1,
    "Role-interaction model" = m2
  ),
  \(model, model_name) {
    r2 <- performance::r2_nakagawa(model)

    tibble(
      Model = model_name,
      `Marginal R2` = r2$R2_marginal,
      `Conditional R2` = r2$R2_conditional
    )
  }
)

tab_s3 <- tibble(
  Model = c(
    "Null model",
    "Additive model",
    "Role-interaction model"
  ),
  AIC = c(AIC(m0), AIC(m1), AIC(m2)),
  BIC = c(BIC(m0), BIC(m1), BIC(m2)),
  `Likelihood-ratio chi-square` = c(
    NA,
    lrt_s2$Chisq[2],
    lrt_s2$Chisq[3]
  ),
  df = c(
    NA,
    lrt_s2$`Chi Df`[2],
    lrt_s2$`Chi Df`[3]
  ),
  p = c(
    NA,
    lrt_s2$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2],
    lrt_s2$`Pr(>Chisq)`[3]
  )
) |>
  left_join(r2_s2, by = "Model") |>
  mutate(
    AIC = round(AIC),
    BIC = round(BIC),
    `Likelihood-ratio chi-square` =
      round(`Likelihood-ratio chi-square`, 2),
    `Marginal R2` = round(`Marginal R2`, 3),
    `Conditional R2` = round(`Conditional R2`, 3),
    p = case_when(
      is.na(p) ~ "",
      p < .001 ~ "<.001",
      TRUE ~ sprintf("%.3f", p)
    )
  )

# Publication-ready table
table_s3 <- flextable(tab_s3) |>
  set_header_labels(
    Model = "Model",
    AIC = "AIC",
    BIC = "BIC",
    `Likelihood-ratio chi-square` = "χ²",
    df = "df",
    p = "P",
    `Marginal R2` = "Marginal R²",
    `Conditional R2` = "Conditional R²"
  ) |>
  border_remove() |>
  hline_top(
    part = "header",
    border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 1)
  ) |>
  hline_bottom(
    part = "header",
    border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 0.75)
  ) |>
  hline_bottom(
    part = "body",
    border = fp_border(color = "black", width = 1)
  ) |>
  font(fontname = "Arial", part = "all") |>
  fontsize(size = 9, part = "all") |>
  bold(part = "header") |>
  align(j = "Model", align = "left", part = "all") |>
  align(j = 2:ncol(tab_s3), align = "center", part = "all") |>
  padding(
    padding.top = 2,
    padding.bottom = 2,
    padding.left = 3,
    padding.right = 3,
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  autofit()

save_as_docx(
  table_s3,
  path = file.path(output_dir, "Table_S3.docx")
)
```

## Overall and role-specific associations  

```{r s2-effects}

# Effects are average marginal effects on the probability scale.
# Continuous predictors represent a 1-SD increase; binary predictors
# compare 1 with 0.

struct_vars <- list(
  income_filled_z = 1,
  age_z = 1,
  is_employed = "reference",
  gender_bin = c(0, 1)
)

eff_space_overall <- avg_comparisons(
  m2,
  variables = struct_vars,
  type = "response"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(role = "Overall")

eff_space_role <- avg_comparisons(
  m2,
  variables = struct_vars,
  by = "behaviour_role",
  type = "response"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(role = as.character(behaviour_role))

eff_space <- bind_rows(
  eff_space_overall,
  eff_space_role
) |>
  mutate(
    Predictor = unname(clean_names[term]),
    across(
      c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
      ~ .x * 100,
      .names = "{.col}_pp"
    ),
    # For the overall estimate only, convert the probability difference
    # into the expected difference in number of relevant actions out of 18.
    actions = if_else(
      role == "Overall",
      estimate * 18,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

eff_space |>
  select(
    Predictor,
    contrast,
    role,
    estimate_pp,
    conf.low_pp,
    conf.high_pp,
    actions
  ) |>
  print(n = 50)

```

## Income-as-factor sensitivity for Figure 2

The primary analysis treats the ordered income categories as a standardised
linear predictor and retains non-response with a missingness indicator. As a
functional-form check for Figure 2 only, the following models use respondents
with observed income and compare that linear specification with a categorical
income-by-role specification. All other structural predictors and their role
interactions are retained.

```{r s2-income-factor-sensitivity}
df_income_factor <- df_long |>
  filter(!is.na(income)) |>
  drop_na(is_relevant, age_z, gender_bin, is_employed, behaviour_role) |>
  mutate(
    income_factor = factor(
      income,
      levels = 1:10,
      labels = income_labels
    )
  )

m_income_linear_sensitivity <- glmmTMB(
  is_relevant ~
    (age_z + gender_bin + income_z + is_employed) * behaviour_role +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = binomial("logit"),
  data = df_income_factor
)

m_income_factor_sensitivity <- glmmTMB(
  is_relevant ~
    (age_z + gender_bin + income_factor + is_employed) * behaviour_role +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = binomial("logit"),
  data = df_income_factor
)

income_factor_lrt <- anova(
  m_income_linear_sensitivity,
  m_income_factor_sensitivity
) |>
  as.data.frame()

income_factor_comparison <- tibble(
  model = c("Income linear", "Income categorical"),
  n_respondents = n_distinct(df_income_factor$response_id),
  n_person_actions = nrow(df_income_factor),
  AIC = c(AIC(m_income_linear_sensitivity), AIC(m_income_factor_sensitivity)),
  BIC = c(BIC(m_income_linear_sensitivity), BIC(m_income_factor_sensitivity)),
  lrt_chisq = c(NA_real_, income_factor_lrt$Chisq[2]),
  lrt_df = c(NA_real_, income_factor_lrt$`Chi Df`[2]),
  lrt_p = c(NA_real_, income_factor_lrt$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2])
)

income_factor_predictions <- avg_predictions(
  m_income_factor_sensitivity,
  by = c("income_factor", "behaviour_role"),
  type = "response"
) |>
  as_tibble()

income_factor_counts <- df_income_factor |>
  distinct(response_id, income_factor) |>
  count(income_factor, name = "n_respondents")

income_factor_trend <- income_factor_predictions |>
  mutate(income_rank = as.integer(income_factor)) |>
  group_by(behaviour_role) |>
  summarise(
    spearman_rho = cor(income_rank, estimate, method = "spearman"),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Keep all sensitivity-check results in the rendered analysis rather than
# writing intermediate CSV files.
income_factor_comparison |>
  mutate(
    delta_AIC = AIC - min(AIC),
    delta_BIC = BIC - min(BIC)
  )
income_factor_counts
income_factor_trend
income_factor_predictions |> print(n = Inf)
```

The categorical specification improves the unpenalised fit relative to the
linear specification (likelihood-ratio χ²(`r income_factor_lrt[["Chi Df"]][2]`) =
`r sprintf("%.2f", income_factor_lrt$Chisq[2])`,
*p* = `r format.pval(income_factor_lrt[["Pr(>Chisq)"]][2], digits = 3)`), which
suggests some departure from a perfectly linear association. However, it adds
`r income_factor_lrt[["Chi Df"]][2]` parameters, and the continuous model has the
lower AIC by `r sprintf("%.1f", diff(income_factor_comparison$AIC))` points and
the lower BIC by `r sprintf("%.1f", diff(income_factor_comparison$BIC))` points.
The category-specific predictions also retain a broadly increasing ordinal
pattern across roles (Spearman correlations =
`r paste0(sprintf("%.2f", range(income_factor_trend$spearman_rho)), collapse = " to ")`),
while the smallest income category contains only
`r min(income_factor_counts$n_respondents)` respondents. We therefore retain
standardised income as a continuous predictor in Figure 2: it captures the
main gradient much more parsimoniously and yields more stable estimates,
while the factor analysis documents the limited evidence for nonlinearity.

# Utilisation of the opportunity space

Utilisation is defined as the share of actions in a respondent's opportunity
space that they have already taken. Descriptively, this is summarised at the
person level. Inferential analyses retain the person-action structure and are
estimated on all relevant actions.

```{r s3-population}
message(
  "Share of person-action observations in utilisation analyses: ",
  round(nrow(df_relevant) / nrow(df_long), 3)
)

# Person-level descriptive statistics
tab_utilisation <- df_person |>
  summarise(
    n = sum(!is.na(utilisation_share)),
    mean = mean(utilisation_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(utilisation_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(utilisation_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    q25 = quantile(utilisation_share, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
    q75 = quantile(utilisation_share, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

tab_utilisation

# Descriptive utilisation by role
tab_utilisation_role <- df_relevant |>
  group_by(response_id, behaviour_role) |>
  summarise(
    n_relevant = n(),
    n_taken = sum(is_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    utilisation_share = mean(is_taken, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  group_by(behaviour_role) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(utilisation_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(utilisation_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(utilisation_share, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

tab_utilisation_role
```

## Predictors of utilisation, overall and by role

The outcome is whether an action within the respondent's opportunity space has
already been taken. Effects are expressed as percentage-point differences in
the probability that a relevant action has been taken.

```{r s3-models}
preds_sociodem <- c(
  "income_filled_z",
  "age_z",
  "gender_bin"
)

# Utilisation:
# QoL is excluded because ratings refer to experienced impact for actions
# already taken and expected impact for relevant actions not yet taken.
preds_psych_util <- c(
  "conversation_z",
  "action_knowledge_z",
  "attribution_z",
  "techno_optimism_z",
  "political_z"
)

preds_util <- c(
  preds_sociodem,
  preds_psych_util
)

# Perceived opportunity and motivation:
# These analyses are restricted to relevant actions not yet taken, so QoL
# always refers to expected quality-of-life impact.
preds_psych_untaken <- c(
  "qol_expected_z",
  "conversation_z",
  "action_knowledge_z",
  "attribution_z",
  "techno_optimism_z",
  "political_z"
)

preds_untaken <- c(
  preds_sociodem,
  preds_psych_untaken
)

eff_taken <- 
  fit_effects(
    df_relevant,
    "is_taken",
    preds_util,
    family = "binomial"
  )

eff_taken <- eff_taken |>
  mutate(
    construct = construct_levels[1],
    across(
      c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
      ~ .x * 100,
      .names = "{.col}_pp"
    )
  )

eff_taken |>
  filter(level == "Overall") |>
  select(
    Predictor,
    estimate_pp,
    conf.low_pp,
    conf.high_pp
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(estimate_pp))
```

## Income: technology adoption versus curtailment

Examining income differences in curtailment vs technology adoption.

```{r s3-income-contrast}
# Refit the income model underlying the primary utilisation analysis so that
# the technology-versus-curtailment difference can be tested directly.

df_income_util <- df_relevant |>
  drop_na(
    is_taken,
    income_filled_z,
    gender_bin,
    age_z,
    income_status
  )

m_income_util <- glmmTMB(
  is_taken ~
    income_filled_z * behaviour_role +
    gender_bin +
    age_z +
    income_status +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = binomial("logit"),
  data = df_income_util
)

inc_by_role <- avg_comparisons(
  m_income_util,
  variables = "income_filled_z",
  by = "behaviour_role",
  type = "response"
)

inc_by_role_pp <- inc_by_role |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
      ~ .x * 100,
      .names = "{.col}_pp"
    )
  )

inc_by_role_pp |>
  select(
    behaviour_role,
    estimate_pp,
    conf.low_pp,
    conf.high_pp
  )

# Test whether the income association differs between consumer technology
# adoption and consumer curtailment.
stopifnot(
  as.character(inc_by_role$behaviour_role[1]) ==
    "Consumer (technology)",
  as.character(inc_by_role$behaviour_role[2]) ==
    "Consumer (curtailment)"
)

inc_tech_vs_curt <- avg_comparisons(
  m_income_util,
  variables = "income_filled_z",
  by = "behaviour_role",
  type = "response",
  hypothesis = "b1 - b2 = 0"
)

inc_tech_vs_curt
```

## Sensitivity: action uptake without conditioning on opportunity

The primary analysis conditions on respondents' classification of an action as
part of their opportunity space. As a sensitivity analysis, we repeat the
analysis across all 18 actions. This analysis does not depend on how many
untaken actions respondents classify as not relevant, but it combines
opportunity and utilisation and is therefore not treated as the primary
measure of utilisation.

```{r s3-sensitivity-all-actions}
df_all_taken <- df_long |>
  mutate(
    is_taken_all = as.integer(
      action_status == "Already taken"
    )
  )

eff_taken_all <- 
  fit_effects(
    df_all_taken,
    "is_taken_all",
    preds_util,
    family = "binomial"
  )

eff_taken_all <- eff_taken_all |>
  mutate(
    across(
      c(estimate, conf.low, conf.high),
      ~ .x * 100,
      .names = "{.col}_pp"
    )
  )

# Inspect overall sensitivity estimates
eff_taken_all |>
  filter(level == "Overall") |>
  select(
    Predictor,
    estimate_pp,
    conf.low_pp,
    conf.high_pp
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(estimate_pp))


### Supplementary Table 7: sensitivity to conditioning on opportunity
```

# Perceived opportunity and motivation for untaken actions

Analyses are restricted to actions that respondents classified as relevant but
had not yet taken. Perceived opportunity captures respondents' perceived ability to undertake
actions they already consider relevant. It excludes actions classified as not relevant.

## Predictors of perceived opportunity and motivation

Separate multilevel models are estimated for perceived opportunity and
motivation among relevant, untaken actions. QoL is expected quality-of-life impact in these models because the
analytical sample is restricted to relevant actions not yet taken.

```{r s4-models}
eff_opp <- fit_effects(
  df_untaken,
  "opportunity",
  preds_untaken,
  family = "gaussian"
) |>
  mutate(
    construct = "Perceived opportunity"
  )

eff_mot <- fit_effects(
  df_untaken,
  "motivation",
  preds_untaken,
  family = "gaussian"
) |>
  mutate(
    construct = "Motivation"
  )

effects_s4 <- bind_rows(
  eff_opp,
  eff_mot
) |>
  mutate(
    construct = factor(
      construct,
      levels = c(
        "Perceived opportunity",
        "Motivation"
      )
    )
  )

# Overall estimates
effects_s4 |>
  filter(level == "Overall") |>
  select(
    construct,
    Predictor,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) |>
  arrange(
    construct,
    desc(estimate)
  ) |>
  print(n = 30)
```

## Sensitivity analysis: climate conversations and overlapping social-role action
Action 15 ("Talk with family/friends about climate action") overlaps conceptually with the 
climate-conversations predictor, which includes the frequency with which climate change 
or climate action is discussed with family/household and friends/acquaintances. 
We therefore re-estimate the climate-conversations associations after excluding action 15.

This sensitivity analysis assesses whether the overall association and, especially, 
the association for social role-model actions are driven by this item overlap.

## Within-person coupling between perceived opportunity and motivation

Perceived opportunity and motivation are conceptually distinct: being able to
take an action does not imply being motivated to take it. However, respondents'
perceptions of their opportunities may be related to their motivation. We
therefore test whether, within individuals, actions perceived as more feasible
than their other relevant, untaken actions are also rated as more motivating.

```{r s4-coupling}
df_coupling <- df_untaken |>
  filter(
    !is.na(opportunity),
    !is.na(motivation)
  ) |>
  group_by(response_id) |>
  mutate(
    opportunity_person_mean = mean(
      opportunity,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    opportunity_within = opportunity -
      opportunity_person_mean
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    # Standardise the within-person deviation and person mean separately.
    # The within-person coefficient therefore corresponds to a 1-SD
    # within-person difference in perceived opportunity.
    opportunity_within_z = as.numeric(
      scale(opportunity_within)
    ),
    opportunity_person_mean_z = as.numeric(
      scale(opportunity_person_mean)
    ),
    motivation_z = as.numeric(
      scale(motivation)
    )
  )

message(
  "Person-action observations in coupling analysis: ",
  nrow(df_coupling)
)

message(
  "Respondents in coupling analysis: ",
  n_distinct(df_coupling$response_id)
)

# Respondents need variation across at least two untaken actions to identify
# the within-person association.
tab_within_information <- df_coupling |>
  group_by(response_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_actions = n(),
    sd_opportunity = sd(opportunity),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  summarise(
    respondents = n(),
    respondents_multiple_actions = sum(n_actions >= 2),
    respondents_with_opportunity_variation =
      sum(n_actions >= 2 & sd_opportunity > 0, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

tab_within_information


# Primary coupling model
m_coupling <- glmmTMB(
  motivation_z ~
    opportunity_within_z +
    opportunity_person_mean_z +
    factor(behaviour_id) +
    (1 | response_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_coupling
)

coupling_overall <- broom.mixed::tidy(
  m_coupling,
  effects = "fixed",
  conf.int = TRUE
) |>
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "opportunity_within_z",
      "opportunity_person_mean_z"
    )
  )

coupling_overall
```

```{r s4-coupling-role}
m_coupling_role <- glmmTMB(

    factor(behaviour_id) +
    opportunity_person_mean_z +
    opportunity_within_z:behaviour_role +
    (1 | response_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_coupling
)

coupling_role <- broom.mixed::tidy(
  m_coupling_role,
  effects = "fixed",
  conf.int = TRUE
) |>
  filter(
    str_detect(
      term,
      "opportunity_within_z:behaviour_role"
    )
  )

coupling_role
```

### Supplementary Table 9: action-specific opportunity-motivation correlations

```{r s4-table-s9}
tab_s9 <- df_coupling |>
  group_by(
    behaviour_id,
    behaviour_name,
    behaviour_role
  ) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    r = cor(
      opportunity,
      motivation,
      use = "complete.obs",
      method = "pearson"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    fisher_z = atanh(r),
    se_z = 1 / sqrt(n - 3),
    ci_low = tanh(
      fisher_z - 1.96 * se_z
    ),
    ci_high = tanh(
      fisher_z + 1.96 * se_z
    ),
    Action = short_labels[
      as.character(behaviour_id)
    ]
  ) |>
  transmute(
    Action,
    Role = behaviour_role,
    n,
    r,
    `95% CI lower` = ci_low,
    `95% CI upper` = ci_high
  ) |>
  arrange(
    Role,
    desc(r)
  )

table_s9 <- flextable(tab_s9) |>
```

# Expected and experienced quality-of-life impacts

This section compares expected quality-of-life impacts for relevant, untaken
actions with experienced impacts for actions respondents have already taken.

## Expected and experienced quality-of-life impacts

Create an analysis sample containing relevant actions for which respondents
either reported an expected quality-of-life impact or an experienced
quality-of-life impact.

```{r s5-population}
df_qol <- df_long |>
  filter(
    action_status != "Not relevant",
    !is.na(qol)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    taken = as.integer(
      action_status == "Already taken"
    ),
    qol_status = factor(
      if_else(
        taken == 1,
        "Experienced",
        "Expected"
      ),
      levels = c(
        "Expected",
        "Experienced"
      )
    )
  )

message(
  "Person-action observations in quality-of-life analyses: ",
  nrow(df_qol)
)

message(
  "Respondents contributing to quality-of-life analyses: ",
  n_distinct(df_qol$response_id)
)

df_qol |>
  count(qol_status)
```

### Descriptive ratings by action and status

```{r s5-descriptives}
tab_qol_action_raw <- df_qol |>
  group_by(
    behaviour_id,
    behaviour_name,
    behaviour_role,
    qol_status
  ) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(qol, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd = sd(qol, na.rm = TRUE),
    median = median(qol, na.rm = TRUE),
    se = sd / sqrt(n),
    conf.low = mean - qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    conf.high = mean + qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * se,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(
    behaviour_id,
    qol_status
  )

tab_qol_action_raw

# Raw descriptive means and confidence intervals for Figure 4 and Table S10
qol_levels_action_raw <- tab_qol_action_raw |>
  transmute(
    behaviour_id = as.integer(as.character(behaviour_id)),
    action = short_labels[as.character(behaviour_id)],
    role = as.character(behaviour_role),
    qol_status,
    n,
    estimate = mean,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  )
```

### Covariate-adjusted between-person model

The model estimates experienced-minus-expected differences for each action,
adjusting for income, age and gender and accounting for repeated observations
within respondents. The descriptive ratings shown in Figure 4 are raw means.

```{r s5-between-model}
df_qol_between <- df_qol |>
  drop_na(
    qol,
    income_filled_z,
    age_z,
    gender_bin
  )

m_qol_between <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    qol_status * factor(behaviour_id) +
    income_filled_z +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    (1 | response_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_between
)
```

### Adjusted experienced-minus-expected differences

```{r s5-between-differences}
qol_between_gap <- avg_comparisons(
  m_qol_between,
  variables = list(
    qol_status = c(
      "Expected",
      "Experienced"
    )
  ),
  by = "behaviour_id"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    behaviour_id = as.integer(
      as.character(behaviour_id)
    ),
    action = short_labels[
      as.character(behaviour_id)
    ]
  )

qol_between_gap |>
  select(
    behaviour_id,
    action,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) |>
  arrange(behaviour_id)
```

### Overall adjusted difference

```{r s5-between-overall}
qol_between_overall <- avg_comparisons(
  m_qol_between,
  variables = list(
    qol_status = c(
      "Expected",
      "Experienced"
    )
  )
) |>
  as_tibble()

qol_between_overall
```

The estimates above are adjusted between-person comparisons. They compare
respondents who have taken an action with respondents for whom the same action
remains untaken and therefore do not estimate the effect of taking the action.


## Within-person difference in quality-of-life ratings

The between-person comparison may partly reflect stable differences between respondents. 
We therefore decomposed action status into each respondent's proportion of relevant actions 
already taken and the deviation of each action's status from this respondent-level mean.
The within-person coefficient compares quality-of-life ratings for taken and untaken actions 
within the same respondent, while action fixed effects account for systematic differences 
in ratings between actions. This controls for stable respondent-level differences but remains 
observational because respondents may selectively take actions they already expect to affect
their quality of life more positively.

```{r s5-within-data}
df_qol_within <- df_qol |>
  group_by(response_id) |>
  mutate(
    taken_person_mean = mean(
      taken,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    taken_within = taken -
      taken_person_mean
  ) |>
  ungroup()

tab_qol_within_information <- df_qol_within |>
  group_by(response_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_actions = n(),
    n_taken = sum(taken == 1),
    n_untaken = sum(taken == 0),
    has_within_variation =
      any(taken == 1) &
      any(taken == 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  summarise(
    respondents = n(),
    respondents_within_variation =
      sum(has_within_variation)
  )

tab_qol_within_information
```

### Overall within-person model

Action fixed effects account for systematic differences in quality-of-life
ratings between the 18 actions.

```{r s5-within-model}
m_qol_within <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    taken_within +
    taken_person_mean +
    factor(behaviour_id) +
    (1 | response_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_within
)

qol_within_overall <- broom.mixed::tidy(
  m_qol_within,
  effects = "fixed",
  conf.int = TRUE
) |>
  filter(
    term %in% c(
      "taken_within",
      "taken_person_mean"
    )
  )

qol_within_overall
```

The coefficient for taken_person_mean captures the between-person association between 
respondents' overall proportion of relevant actions already taken and their quality-of-life ratings, 
conditional on the within-person action-status component and action fixed effects.

## Sensitivity to adjustment for psychological and social characteristics

The primary between-person model adjusts for income, age and gender. As a
sensitivity analysis, we additionally adjust for perceived action knowledge,
climate conversations, individual-attribution belief, techno-optimism and
political orientation. Because adding these covariates can change the analysis
sample through missingness, the demographic and fully adjusted specifications
are compared on the same complete-case sample. This analysis is a robustness
check rather than a preferred causal specification, because some of the
additional covariates may themselves be related to prior climate action.

```{r s5-sensitivity-data}
df_qol_sensitivity <- df_qol_between |>
  filter(
    complete.cases(
      action_knowledge_z,
      conversation_z,
      attribution_z,
      techno_optimism_z,
      political_z
    )
  ) |>
  droplevels()

message(
  "Person-action observations in QoL sensitivity sample: ",
  nrow(df_qol_sensitivity)
)

message(
  "Respondents in QoL sensitivity sample: ",
  n_distinct(df_qol_sensitivity$response_id)
)
```

### Same-sample demographic and fully adjusted models

```{r s5-sensitivity-models}
m_qol_between_demog_cc <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    qol_status * factor(behaviour_id) +
    income_filled_z +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    (1 | response_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_sensitivity
)

m_qol_between_full_cc <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    qol_status * factor(behaviour_id) +
    income_filled_z +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    action_knowledge_z +
    conversation_z +
    attribution_z +
    techno_optimism_z +
    political_z +
    (1 | response_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_sensitivity
)
```

### Overall sensitivity estimates

```{r s5-sensitivity-overall}
qol_sensitivity_overall <- bind_rows(
  avg_comparisons(
    m_qol_between_demog_cc,
    variables = list(
      qol_status = c(
        "Expected",
        "Experienced"
      )
    )
  ) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      model = "Demographic adjustment"
    ),

  avg_comparisons(
    m_qol_between_full_cc,
    variables = list(
      qol_status = c(
        "Expected",
        "Experienced"
      )
    )
  ) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      model = "Additional psychological adjustment"
    )
) |>
  select(
    model,
    contrast,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  )

qol_sensitivity_overall
```

### Action-specific sensitivity estimates

```{r s5-sensitivity-action}
qol_sensitivity_action <- bind_rows(
  avg_comparisons(
    m_qol_between_demog_cc,
    variables = list(
      qol_status = c(
        "Expected",
        "Experienced"
      )
    ),
    by = "behaviour_id"
  ) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      model = "Demographic adjustment"
    ),

  avg_comparisons(
    m_qol_between_full_cc,
    variables = list(
      qol_status = c(
        "Expected",
        "Experienced"
      )
    ),
    by = "behaviour_id"
  ) |>
    as_tibble() |>
    mutate(
      model = "Additional psychological adjustment"
    )
) |>
  mutate(
    behaviour_id = as.integer(
      as.character(behaviour_id)
    ),
    action = short_labels[
      as.character(behaviour_id)
    ]
  ) |>
  select(
    behaviour_id,
    action,
    model,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) |>
  arrange(
    behaviour_id,
    model
  )

qol_sensitivity_action |>
  print(n = 36)



```

The sensitivity analysis should be interpreted by comparing the same-sample
estimates above. A similar estimate after additional adjustment indicates that
the expected-experienced difference is not readily accounted for by the
measured psychological and social characteristics. It does not remove
action-specific selection into taking an action and therefore does not identify
a causal effect of action uptake.

## Socioeconomic differences in quality-of-life impacts

```{r}
# Expected QoL: actions in the remaining opportunity space
df_qol_expected_income <- df_qol |>
  filter(qol_status == "Expected") |>
  drop_na(
    qol,
    income_filled_z,
    income_status,
    age_z,
    gender_bin,
    behaviour_role
  ) |>
  droplevels()

m_qol_expected_income_role <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    income_filled_z * behaviour_role +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_expected_income
)

# Overall and role-specific income associations with expected QoL
qol_expected_income_overall <- avg_slopes(
  m_qol_expected_income_role,
  variables = "income_filled_z"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    qol_status = "Expected",
    level = "Overall"
  )

qol_expected_income_role <- avg_slopes(
  m_qol_expected_income_role,
  variables = "income_filled_z",
  by = "behaviour_role"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    qol_status = "Expected",
    level = as.character(behaviour_role)
  )


# Experienced QoL: actions already taken
df_qol_experienced_income <- df_qol |>
  filter(qol_status == "Experienced") |>
  drop_na(
    qol,
    income_filled_z,
    income_status,
    age_z,
    gender_bin,
    behaviour_role
  ) |>
  droplevels()

m_qol_experienced_income_role <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    income_filled_z * behaviour_role +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_experienced_income
)

# Overall and role-specific income associations with experienced QoL
qol_experienced_income_overall <- avg_slopes(
  m_qol_experienced_income_role,
  variables = "income_filled_z"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    qol_status = "Experienced",
    level = "Overall"
  )

qol_experienced_income_role <- avg_slopes(
  m_qol_experienced_income_role,
  variables = "income_filled_z",
  by = "behaviour_role"
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    qol_status = "Experienced",
    level = as.character(behaviour_role)
  )


# Combine income estimates
qol_income_results <- bind_rows(
  qol_expected_income_overall,
  qol_expected_income_role,
  qol_experienced_income_overall,
  qol_experienced_income_role
) |>
  select(
    qol_status,
    level,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high,
    p.value
  ) |>
  arrange(
    factor(
      qol_status,
      levels = c(
        "Expected",
        "Experienced"
      )
    ),
    factor(
      level,
      levels = c(
        "Overall",
        role_levels
      )
    )
  )

qol_income_results


# Formal tests of whether income associations differ across roles
#
# Compare the interaction models above with otherwise identical models
# assuming a common income association across roles.

m_qol_expected_income_common <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    income_filled_z +
    behaviour_role +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_expected_income
)

m_qol_experienced_income_common <- glmmTMB(
  qol ~
    income_filled_z +
    behaviour_role +
    income_status +
    age_z +
    gender_bin +
    (1 | response_id) +
    (1 | behaviour_id),
  family = gaussian(),
  data = df_qol_experienced_income
)

income_role_test_expected <- anova(
  m_qol_expected_income_common,
  m_qol_expected_income_role
)

income_role_test_experienced <- anova(
  m_qol_experienced_income_common,
  m_qol_experienced_income_role
)

income_role_test_expected
income_role_test_experienced


# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
```

## Supplementary Table 10: expected and experienced quality-of-life impacts

Supplementary Table 10 reports raw mean expected and experienced ratings and
the covariate-adjusted between-person difference for each action. The overall
within-person estimate is reported separately in the main text because it is a
different estimand and is not action-specific.

```{r s5-table-s10}
tab_s10 <- qol_levels_action_raw |>
  select(
    behaviour_id,
    action,
    qol_status,
    estimate,
    conf.low,
    conf.high
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = qol_status,
    values_from = c(
      estimate,
      conf.low,
      conf.high
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(
    qol_between_gap |>
      select(
        behaviour_id,
        between = estimate,
        between_low = conf.low,
        between_high = conf.high
      ),
    by = "behaviour_id"
  ) |>
  arrange(behaviour_id) |>
  transmute(
    Action = action,
    `Expected QoL (raw mean)` = sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)",
      estimate_Expected,
      conf.low_Expected,
      conf.high_Expected
    ),
    `Experienced QoL (raw mean)` = sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)",
      estimate_Experienced,
      conf.low_Experienced,
      conf.high_Experienced
    ),
    `Adjusted between-person difference` = sprintf(
      "%.2f (%.2f, %.2f)",
      between,
      between_low,
      between_high
    )
  )

table_s10 <- flextable(tab_s10) |>
  border_remove() |>
  hline_top(
    part = "header",
    border = fp_border(
      color = "black",
      width = 1
    )
  ) |>
  hline_bottom(
    part = "header",
    border = fp_border(
      color = "black",
      width = 0.75
    )
  ) |>
  hline_bottom(
    part = "body",
    border = fp_border(
      color = "black",
      width = 1
    )
  ) |>
  bold(part = "header") |>
  align(
    j = 2:4,
    align = "center",
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  font(
    fontname = "Arial",
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  fontsize(
    size = 9,
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  padding(
    padding.top = 2,
    padding.bottom = 2,
    padding.left = 3,
    padding.right = 3,
    part = "all"
  ) |>
  autofit()

save_as_docx(
  table_s10,
  path = file.path(
    output_dir,
    "Table_S10.docx"
  )
)

table_s10
```

# Figures

Figures 1-4 and Supplementary Fig. 1 are produced in two steps.

1. **Data export (R).** The chunk below writes the data behind each figure to
   `figures/`: a JSON file read by the renderer, the same data as a `.js` file
   for the browser preview, and CSV source data. No models are refitted; every
   estimate is reused from the analyses above, and every statistic shown in a
   figure is computed here.
2. **Drawing (JavaScript).** The renderer (written to `figures/` by the
   `figure-renderer` chunk) draws each figure as SVG at
   183 mm width (7 pt text, 6 pt tick labels, 8 pt panel letters). It contains
   no statistics. The SVGs are then converted to vector PDF and 600-dpi PNG.

Requirements for step 2: [Node.js](https://nodejs.org) (any current version,
no packages needed) and, for PDF/PNG, the R package `rsvg`. Without Node.js the
figures can still be previewed and saved from `figures/figures.html`.

## Figure data

```{r figure-data}
figure_keys <- c("1", "2", "3", "4", "S1")

# Display order of the 18 actions in every figure: grouped by role, in survey
# order within each role. The renderer draws rows in exactly this order.
figure_action_order <- c(
  1L, 2L, 6L,                # Consumer (technology)
  3L, 4L, 5L, 7L, 8L, 9L,    # Consumer (curtailment)
  12L, 13L,                  # Organisational participant
  10L,                       # Investor
  11L, 16L, 17L, 18L,        # Citizen
  14L, 15L                   # Social role model
)

figure_actions <- df_long |>
  distinct(behaviour_id, behaviour_role) |>
  transmute(
    behaviour_id = as.integer(as.character(behaviour_id)),
    action       = unname(short_labels[as.character(behaviour_id)]),
    role         = as.character(behaviour_role)
  )

stopifnot(
  nrow(figure_actions) == 18L,
  !anyDuplicated(figure_action_order),
  setequal(figure_actions$behaviour_id, figure_action_order),
  !anyNA(figure_actions$action),
  # each role must occupy one contiguous block in the display order
  length(rle(figure_actions$role[match(figure_action_order,
                                       figure_actions$behaviour_id)])$values) ==
    length(role_levels)
)

# Attach action label and role, and sort rows into display order.
in_figure_order <- function(d) {
  d |>
    mutate(behaviour_id = as.integer(as.character(behaviour_id))) |>
    left_join(figure_actions, by = "behaviour_id") |>
    arrange(match(behaviour_id, figure_action_order)) |>
    relocate(behaviour_id, action, role)
}

# Mean with a 95% t confidence interval.
mean_ci <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!is.na(x)]
  n <- length(x)
  m <- mean(x)
  h <- if (n > 1) qt(0.975, df = n - 1) * sd(x) / sqrt(n) else NA_real_
  tibble(n = n, mean = m, low = m - h, high = m + h)
}

# Write <key>_data.json (renderer), <key>_data.js (browser preview) and
# CSV source data (one file per named table).
write_figure_data <- function(key, data, source_data) {
  json <- jsonlite::toJSON(data, auto_unbox = TRUE, dataframe = "rows",
                           digits = NA, na = "null", pretty = TRUE)
  stem <- file.path(figure_dir, paste0("Figure_", key))
  writeLines(enc2utf8(as.character(json)), paste0(stem, "_data.json"), useBytes = TRUE)
  writeLines(
    enc2utf8(c("window.FIGURE_DATA = window.FIGURE_DATA || {};",
               paste0("window.FIGURE_DATA[\"", key, "\"] = ", json, ";"))),
    paste0(stem, "_data.js"), useBytes = TRUE
  )
  for (nm in names(source_data)) {
    readr::write_csv(source_data[[nm]],
                     paste0(stem, "_source_data_", nm, ".csv"), na = "")
  }
}

ci_contains_estimate <- function(d) all(d$low <= d$estimate & d$estimate <= d$high)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure 1: opportunity space
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
fig1_hist <- function(x) {
  stopifnot(!anyNA(x), all(x %in% 0:18))
  tabulate(as.integer(x) + 1L, nbins = 19L) / length(x)
}

status_key <- c("Already taken"       = "taken",
                "Relevant, not taken" = "untaken",
                "Not relevant"        = "not_relevant")

fig1_items <- df_long |>
  count(behaviour_id, action_status, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(behaviour_id) |>
  mutate(share = n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(behaviour_id,
            status = unname(status_key[as.character(action_status)]),
            share) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = status, values_from = share, values_fill = 0) |>
  in_figure_order() |>
  select(behaviour_id, action, role, taken, untaken, not_relevant)

fig1_hist_tab <- tibble(
  n_actions   = 0:18,
  opportunity = fig1_hist(df_person$opportunity_space),
  taken       = fig1_hist(df_person$n_already_taken),
  remaining   = fig1_hist(df_person$remaining_space)
)

stopifnot(
  nrow(fig1_items) == 18L,
  all(abs(fig1_items$taken + fig1_items$untaken + fig1_items$not_relevant - 1) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(colSums(fig1_hist_tab[, -1]) - 1) < 1e-10)
)

write_figure_data(
  "1",
  list(n_respondents = nrow(df_person),
       hist  = as.list(fig1_hist_tab[, -1]),
       items = fig1_items),
  list(a = fig1_hist_tab |> mutate(across(-n_actions, ~ 100 * .x)) |>
             rename(opportunity_space_pct = opportunity, already_taken_pct = taken,
                    remaining_pct = remaining),
       b = fig1_items |> mutate(across(c(taken, untaken, not_relevant), ~ 100 * .x)) |>
             rename(already_taken_pct = taken, relevant_not_taken_pct = untaken,
                    not_relevant_pct = not_relevant))
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure 2a: opportunity space by income category (descriptive)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Axis labels give the lower bound of each income category in DKK, with an
# approximate EUR equivalent rounded to the nearest EUR 5,000.
dkk_per_eur      <- 7.46
income_lower_dkk <- c(200000, 300000, 400000, 500000, 650000, 800000,
                      1000000, 1250000, 1500000)
big     <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 0, big.mark = ",")
to_eur5 <- function(x) round(x / dkk_per_eur / 5000) * 5000
euro    <- "\u20ac"

income_axis <- tibble(
  income    = 1:10,
  label_dkk = c(paste0("<", big(income_lower_dkk[1])),
                big(income_lower_dkk[1:8]),
                paste0(big(income_lower_dkk[9]), "+")),
  label_eur = c(paste0("(<", euro, big(to_eur5(income_lower_dkk[1])), ")"),
                paste0("(", euro, big(to_eur5(income_lower_dkk[1:8])), ")"),
                paste0("(", euro, big(to_eur5(income_lower_dkk[9])), "+)"))
)
stopifnot(length(income_labels) == nrow(income_axis))

fig2a <- df_person |>
  filter(!is.na(income)) |>
  group_by(income) |>
  summarise(
    n           = n(),
    opportunity = mean_ci(opportunity_space),
    taken       = mean_ci(n_already_taken),
    remaining   = mean_ci(remaining_space),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::unpack(c(opportunity, taken, remaining), names_sep = "_") |>
  select(-ends_with("_n")) |>
  mutate(income = as.integer(income)) |>
  left_join(income_axis, by = "income") |>
  relocate(income, label_dkk, label_eur, n)

stopifnot(
  nrow(fig2a) == 10L,
  sum(fig2a$n) == sum(!is.na(df_person$income)),
  !anyNA(fig2a)
)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Figure 2b-d: adjusted associations (same estimates as Supplementary Table 4)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Overall estimates are also expressed as a difference in the expected number
# of actions in the opportunity space out of 18.
fig2bcd <- eff_space |>
  filter(term %in% c("income_filled_z", "is_employed", "age_z")) |>
  transmute(
    term,
    predictor    = Predictor,
    role         = as.character(role),
    actions      = if_else(role == "Overall", 18 * estimate,  NA_real_),
    actions_low  = if_else(role == "Overall", 18 * conf.low,  NA_real_),
    actions_high = if_else(role == "Overall", 18 * conf.high, NA_real_),
    estimate     = estimate_pp,

stopifnot(

write_figure_data(

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

fig3_predictors <- tibble(
```
